verdicts.claim: There are four checkpoint modes: PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE. PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting
verdicts.evidence: c3ref lists all four; PASSIVE: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked ... might leave the checkpoint unfinished'. Note: wal.html itself says 'three subtypes' (omits TRUNCATE).

verdicts.claim: FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE block until no writer is active and all readers use the latest snapshot. They also take the exclusive writer lock
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE 'also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock'; wal.html: 'FULL and RESTART ... can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()', automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE.

verdicts.claim: RESTART adds a wait until all readers read from the database file only, so the next writer restarts the WAL from the beginning. TRUNCATE adds truncation
verdicts.evidence: c3ref RESTART/TRUNCATE text matches; wal.html: 'readers might block while the checkpoint is running'. Minor tension: c3ref says RESTART 'does not impede readers'.

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint can run beside readers, but it stops before any WAL page that a current reader still needs. It records its progress in the wal-index
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume ... on the next invocation.'

verdicts.claim: After a fully checkpointed WAL and no active readers, the next writer rewinds the WAL to the start and reuses it. A plain checkpoint does not shrink
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)... start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.'

verdicts.claim: After a successful TRUNCATE checkpoint, the WAL file is zero bytes and both pnLog and pnCkpt are zero
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.'

verdicts.claim: A TRUNCATE checkpoint that returns SQLITE_BUSY leaves the WAL at its previous size
verdicts.evidence: Implied, not stated outright: c3ref truncates 'just prior to a successful return' and a BUSY result 'proceeds ... same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE'. PhotoStructure does not address this.

verdicts.claim: If at least one reader is always active and the readers overlap, no checkpoint completes and the WAL grows without bound. The SQLite docs
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete ... avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps"'.

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint cannot reset the WAL in the middle of a write transaction. A long write transaction, such as a large VACUUM, can make
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction'; PhotoStructure: 'The entire rebuilt database gets written to the WAL file'.

verdicts.claim: A Syncthing developer observed that a timer-based application checkpointer may never find a moment with no active reader
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing post (2026-02-06, bt90): 'we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'; 'truncating the WAL requires no active readers/writers'.

verdicts.claim: Syncthing poster proposes accepting an exclusive lock for WAL truncation once the WAL reaches multiple gigabytes. Litestream avoids
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing: 'critical levels of multiple gigabytes ... would mandate some kind of exclusive locking'; Litestream: 'first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint', TRUNCATE above 121,359 pages.

verdicts.claim: PhotoStructure says a TRUNCATE checkpoint after VACUUM reclaims WAL disk space. A 2022-era SQLite forum thread, seen only as a snip
verdicts.evidence: The PhotoStructure half is supported. The 2022 forum-thread half has no footnote and was self-declared as unfetched, so the gate did not check it.
